- Brown necrotic areas at the leaf edges
- V-shaped yellowing pattern widest at margins
- Dark scattered spots on the leaf surface
- Green center remaining

This pattern strongly suggests Verticillium Wilt (V-shaped marginal lesions with yellowing) or possibly Early Blight. Let me check a Verticillium Wilt reference.

The Verticillium Wilt reference shows wilting/drooping leaves. The test image shows something slightly different - a leaf with pronounced marginal yellowing in a V-shaped pattern, brown necrotic edges, and scattered dark spots. The marginal yellowing pattern (widest at margin, narrowing inward) and brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing match the Verticillium Wilt description well, even if the reference shows a different presentation.

The dark scattered spots on the test leaf could represent secondary lesions, but the dominant pattern is the V-shaped marginal chlorosis with necrosis - consistent with Verticillium Wilt.
